title: Little Office of the Holy Ghost for Obtaining the True Love of God
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: Qui procedis ab utroque, Genitore, Genitoque, Spiritus Paraclyte! Redde linguas eloquentes, Sed accende primum mentes Charitatis fomine.
blocks.english:
Thou Who proceedest from both,
The Begetter and the Begotten,
O Spirit, the Paraclete!
Make our tongues eloquent,
But first enkindle our minds
With the kindling of charity.

blocks.source: Fac, o dulcis coeli aura, Corque nostrum sic instaura, Pietatis flammulis, Ut quae fundimus haec vota, Ex amore fluant tota, Sacri plena pneumatis.
blocks.english:
Grant this, O sweet breath of heaven,
And so renew our heart
With the little flames of piety,
That these prayers which we pour forth
May flow wholly from love,
Filled with the Holy Spirit.

blocks.source: ℣. Veni Sancte Spiritus, reple tuorum corda fidelium, et tui amoris ignem in eis accende.
blocks.english: ℣. Come, Holy Ghost, fill the hearts of Thy faithful, and kindle in them the fire of Thy love.
℟. Amen.
℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.
℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.
Hymn

blocks.source: Tu procedens a duobus, Coaequalis es ambobus, Nulla est disparitas; Par Majestas Personarum, Par Potestas singularum, Et communis Deitas.
blocks.english:
Thou, proceeding from the Two,
Art coequal with Them both;
There is no inequality:
Equal is the Majesty of the Persons,
Equal the Power of Each,
And common Their Godhead.

blocks.source: Amor Patris, Filiique, Par amborum, et utrique Gloria consimilis, Coelos imples, terras foves, Mare domas, cuncta moves, Permanens immobilis.
blocks.english:
Love of the Father and the Son,
Equal to Them both, and with glory
Like unto that of Each:
Thou fillest the heavens, cherishest the earth,
Rulest the sea, movest all things,
Thyself remaining unmoved.

blocks.source: ℣. Ure igne, Sancte Spiritus, renes nostros, et cor nostrum Domine.
blocks.english: ℣. Burn with fire, O Holy Ghost, our reins and our heart, O Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Ut tibi casto corpore serviamus, et mundo corde placeamus.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may serve Thee with a chaste body and please Thee with a pure heart.
Prayer

blocks.source: Deus, cui omne cor patet, et omnis voluntas loquitur, et quem nullum latet secretum: purifica per infusionem Sancti Spiritus cogitationes cordis nostri, ut te perfecte diligere et digne laudare mereamur. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum.
blocks.english: O God, unto Whom every heart is open, every will speaketh, and from Whom no secret is hidden: purify the thoughts of our heart by the outpouring of the Holy Ghost, that we may merit perfectly to love Thee and worthily to praise Thee. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.
℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.
℣. Let us bless the Lord.
℟. Thanks be to God.

blocks.source: ℣. Et Fidelium animae per misericordiam Dei requiescant in pace.
blocks.english: ℣. And may the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
℟. Amen.
℣. Come, Holy Ghost, fill, etc.

referenceExpansion.note: Opening invocation and Amen at Matins, p. 100.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.

blocks.source: Tu commutas elementa, Per te sua sacramenta Praestant efficaciam. Tu malignam vim repellis, Tu subvertis et refellis Hostium nequitiam.
Te docente nil obscurum, Te praesente nil impurum, Cuncta sunt splendida; Gloriatur mens jucunda, Per te sana, per te munda, Gaudet conscientia.

blocks.english: ℣. Burn with fire, etc., with the prayer.

blocks.source: Quando venis, corda lenis, Quando subis, atrae nubis Pellitur obscuritas. Sacer ignis pectus uris, Non comburis, sed a curis Eruis, dum visitas.
blocks.english:
When Thou comest, Thou soothest hearts;
When Thou enterest, the darkness
Of the black cloud is driven away.
Holy fire, Thou burnest the breast,
Yet consumest it not, but from cares
Deliverest it when Thou dost visit.

blocks.source: Mentes prius imperitas, Et sopitas et oblitas Instrui et excitas, Cor ad fidem facis pronum, Ori muto reddis sonum, Manans ex te claritas.
blocks.english:
Minds formerly untaught,
Asleep and forgetful,
Thou instructest and awakenest.
Thou makest the heart ready for faith;
Thou restorest speech to the silent mouth,
O brightness flowing forth from Thyself.
℣. Burn with fire, etc., with the prayer.

blocks.source: O quam felix, quam festiva Dies, in qua primitiva Conditur Ecclesia, Sunt primitias jam vivae, Neonatae Matris Divae Tria plebis millia;
blocks.english:
O how happy, how festive
The day on which the infant
Church is founded!
Three thousand of the people
Are now the living first-fruits
Of the newborn holy Mother.

blocks.source: Panes Legis primitivi, Una fiant adoptivi Fide duo populi; Nempes duos unum fecit, Cum duobus se praefecit Lapis caput anguli.
blocks.english:
The first-fruit loaves of the Law:
Let the two peoples become
Adopted children in one faith.
For the Cornerstone made
The two one,
When He set Himself over both.
℣. Burn with fire, etc., with the prayer.

blocks.source: Tu perversos corde vitas, Sed sinceros mente ditas Dono sapientiae, Veritatem notam facis, Et ostendis viam pacis, Semitas justitiae.
blocks.english:
Thou shunnest the perverse of heart,
But enrichest the sincere of mind
With the gift of wisdom.
Thou makest truth known,
And showest the way of peace,
The paths of justice.

blocks.source: Dat liquorem Helisaeus, Largum fundit rorem Deus, Ubi vasa vacua, Utres novi non vetusti Sunt capaces novi musti, Sint et nostra pectora.
blocks.english:
Eliseus giveth the oil;
God poureth forth abundant dew
Where the vessels are empty.
New wineskins, not old,
Can hold the new wine:
Such may our hearts also be.
℣. Burn with fire, etc., with the prayer.

blocks.source: Sed nec musto vel liquore, Nec hoc digni sumus rore, Si discordes moribus. In obscuris vel divis, Sancta nequit Paraclysis Habitare cordibus.
blocks.english:
Yet neither of the new wine, nor the oil,
Nor of this dew are we worthy,
If we are discordant in conduct.
In darkened or divided hearts
The holy Consolation
Cannot dwell.

blocks.source: Consolator ergo veni, Linguas rege, corda leni, Pelle fel et toxica, Nil salubre, nil serenum, Nihil dulce, nihil plenum, Sine tua gratia.
blocks.english:
Come therefore, O Comforter;
Govern our tongues, soothe our hearts,
Drive out gall and poisons.
Nothing is wholesome, nothing serene,
Nothing sweet, nothing full,
Without Thy grace.
℣. Burn with fire, etc., with the prayer.

blocks.source: O ter salubre unguentum! Aquae ditans elementum Sacro in baptismate! Te laudamus mente pura, Prius irae, ex natura, Gratiae nunc filii!
blocks.english:
O thrice-healthful anointing,
Enriching the element of water
In holy Baptism!
We praise Thee with a pure mind,
Formerly by nature children of wrath,
Now children of grace!

blocks.source: Tu quid dator es et donum, Ex quo omne fluit bonum, Cor perfunde gaudio, Tange mentem, purga sordes, Vinclo pacis fac concordes, Jugi sis praesidio.
blocks.english:
Thou Who art both Giver and Gift,
From Whom all good floweth,
Flood our heart with joy.
Touch the mind, cleanse its stains,
Make us one in the bond of peace;
Be our unceasing protection.
℣. Burn with fire, etc., with the prayer.

blocks.english: ℣. Come, Holy Ghost, fill, etc.

referenceExpansion.note: Opening invocation and Amen at Matins, p. 100.

blocks.english: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.
℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.
Hymn

blocks.source: Sicut post Ascensum Christi Rudes linguis inbuisti Varis discipulos, Sic nos vise, sic dignare, Dissidentes congregare, Una fide populos.
blocks.english:
As after the Ascension of Christ
Thou didst instruct the untaught disciples
In diverse tongues,
So visit us; so vouchsafe
To gather differing peoples
Into one faith.

blocks.source: Demum mortis ab hac valle Duc ad vitam recto calle, Laetos de victoria, Ubi Patris, ubi tui, Et aeterni Verbi frui Mereamur gloria.
blocks.english:
At last from this valley of death
Lead us by a straight path to life,
Rejoicing in the victory,
Where we may merit to enjoy
The glory of the Father, of Thyself,
And of the eternal Word.
℣. Burn with fire, etc., with the prayer.

blocks.source: Has ut tela, ergo Horas, Ad te sub Olympi oras Sancte mitto Spiritus! Telis tu remitte tela, Quaeis petatur mens anhela Tuis ab amoribus!
blocks.english:
These Hours, therefore, like arrows,
I send unto Thee beneath the heights of heaven,
O Holy Ghost!
In answer to these arrows send Thine own,
Whereby my yearning mind
May be sought out by Thy love!

blocks.source: Ecce metam, punctum cordis! Vibra, feri: nil hic mortis Est pavendum animae, Centrum peto, tu si petis, Nam ambobus una laetis Meta est victoriae. Amen.
blocks.english:
Behold the mark, the very point of my heart!
Hurl, strike: here no death
Is to be feared by the soul.
I seek the centre, if Thou dost seek it,
For to us both rejoicing
There is one goal of victory. Amen.

editorialNotes.text: The PDF prints “Instrui et excitas” at Prime and “In obscuris vel divis” at None. The English provisionally follows the apparent intended readings “instructest and awakenest” and “in darkened or divided hearts.” The printed Latin is retained; these readings remain pending. Other grammatical irregularities, including “Sunt primitias” and “Tu quid,” are retained in the source column.
